Points, lines and segments (点和线) are all answered with cross products (第13章). orient(a, b, c) = (b − a) × (c − a) tells whether c is left of, on, or right of the line ab. Two segments AB and CD properly cross when C, D lie on opposite sides of AB and A, B on opposite sides of CD; touching or collinear overlaps happen when an orientation is 0 and the point lies inside the other segment's bounding box.

Distance from a point P to a line AB = |(B − A) × (P − A)| / |B − A|. To a segment: if the projection falls outside [A, B] (dot products have the wrong sign), the answer is the distance to the nearer endpoint.
Intersection point of two lines: A + t(B − A) with t = ((C − A) × (D − C)) / ((B − A) × (D − C)).

Hand-made edge cases (crossing, disjoint collinear, overlapping collinear, touching at an endpoint) plus random segments, checked against a Python version that solves for the intersection parameters with exact fractions.
Ray casting; boundary first.

Polygons (多边形): area by the shoelace formula (第13章); point in polygon by ray casting: shoot a ray to the right from the point and count how many edges it crosses; odd = inside. Check "on the boundary" first. Count an edge only if exactly one endpoint is strictly above the ray's line (half-open rule), so a vertex on the ray is not counted twice.
For a convex polygon, binary search over the fan of triangles from vertex 0 answers in O(log n). The polygon may be concave for ray casting.

Two pointers around the hull; diameter.

Rotating calipers (旋转卡壳): on a convex hull, walk two pointers around it together. For each edge i → i+1, advance the opposite pointer j while the triangle (i, i+1, j+1) is larger than (i, i+1, j); then j is the farthest vertex from that edge. Every pointer goes around once: O(n) after the hull.

It gives the diameter (farthest pair, P1452), the minimum width, and the minimum-area enclosing rectangle (P3187): the rectangle always has a side on a hull edge, so try every edge with three pointers (far side, left, right).

Sort by angle; deque; convex polygon intersection.

Half-plane intersection (半平面交): each directed line keeps the region on its left. Sort lines by angle (keep the innermost of parallel lines), then sweep with a deque: before adding a line, pop lines from the back (and front) whose last intersection point falls outside it. At the end, trim the back and front against each other. The remaining lines form the intersection polygon: O(n log n).

Intersection of convex polygons (P4196) = half-plane intersection of all their edges (counter-clockwise, so the inside is on the left). Use doubles with an EPS for "outside", and be ready for an empty or unbounded result (add a big bounding box to keep it bounded).
Three overlapping convex quadrilaterals; the area is checked against clipping one polygon by the others edge by edge (Sutherland–Hodgman) in Python with exact fractions, an independent method.
Circle–line; 3D cross; triple product.

Circles (圆): a point is inside when its distance to the centre is ≤ r; a line meets a circle when its distance to the centre ≤ r, and the two points come from the foot of the perpendicular ± √(r² − d²) along the line.
The circumcircle of three points and the minimum enclosing circle were in 第15章 .

3D geometry (三维几何): the dot product is a·b = axbx + ayby + azbz; the cross product a × b is a vector perpendicular to both, with length = the parallelogram area.
